card.title: Coulomb's law: force between two point charges

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Coulomb's law** gives the force between point charges: $F = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q_1q_2}{r^2}$, along the line joining them — repulsive for like charges, attractive for unlike — with $k = 9\times10^9$ N m²C⁻². NEB 2024's pair (2 μC, 3 μC, 0.1 m) repels at 5.4 N (3m); NEB 2022's MCQ (+2 μC, −3 μC, 0.6 m) gives 0.15 N attractive (1m).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - F = (1/4πε₀) q₁q₂/r²; k = 9×10⁹ N m²C⁻² - ε₀ = 8.85×10⁻¹² C²N⁻¹m⁻² - In medium: F = k q₁q₂/(ε_r r²)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Micro means 10⁻⁶:** 2 μC = 2×10⁻⁶ C — the standard conversion slip.  ·  **Inverse square:** double the distance → force ÷ 4.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A sketched sign convention is part of the data.  ·  A dimensionless ratio still needs the two quantities named.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***NEB 2024*** — 2 μC and 3 μC at 0.1 m: F = 5.4 N repulsive.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Two identical charges 5 cm apart repel with 0.36 N. Find each charge.** — q² = Fr²/k = 0.36 × 0.0025/9×10⁹ = 10⁻¹³ → q = 3.16×10⁻⁷ C ≈ 0.32 μC.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Coulomb's law is Newton's gravitation with charge in place of mass** — plus the possibility of repulsion.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: F = kq₁q₂/r²; k = 9×10⁹ N m²C⁻²; like repel, unlike attract.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The electrostatic force between an electron and proton is ~10³⁹ times their gravitational attraction — gravity is negligible inside atoms.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Doubling r multiplies F by → B  ·  Like charges → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Inverse Square Law of Charge Two centuries before electrons were discovered, Coulomb measured with a torsion balance how charged bodies push and pull: a force proportional to each charge, inversely proportional to the square of the separation. That law is the electrostatic twin of Newton's gravitation.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2022, 2024) ### 2.1 Statement and formula **Coulomb's law:** the electrostatic force between two point charges acts along the line joining them, is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation: $$F = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q_1q_2}{r^2} = k\frac{q_1q_2}{r^2}$$ - $k =…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 83:** the law quantifies the interactions of quantised, conserved charges. - **To Topic 86:** superposition extends the two-charge law to systems. - **To gravitation (Unit 7):** same inverse-square mathematics, different source and strength.

rows.text: Verified PYQs: law + 5.4 N numerical (2024, 3m); 0.15 N attractive MCQ (2022, 1m).  ·  "The force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation."  ·  Why don't we feel electrostatic forces in daily life despite their strength?
